comment.body:
Perceived limitations, whether they originate in honest, careful thinking or paranoid terror, cannot be true. The question whether they are true is ridiculous as long as we refuse to move out of the hypothetical and into the factual because, by definition, the hypothetical only has a place in the absence of fact.

What’s more, there is only one way to obtain facts: doing something. Honestly exposing ourselves to and interacting with what’s really going on.

That means precisely: moving out of the hypothetical and into the actual. We have no facts other than from experience.

This is obvious and easily demonstrable. As soon we allow facts into our mental mix, hypotheticals such as the occult, beliefs, superstitions, delusions, etc., automatically lose their power. You can see this happen with a person in real time. It’s unmistakable. You can watch their mind shift into a completely different, far saner and calmer mode. It’s not hard at all to induce this, except for one thing:

To the degree that a person clings to their infantilism, they will fight against accepting certain facts into their mental mix, even if only to admit them as considerable, let alone consider them honestly.

The reason for this has nothing at all to do with what’s “really real” or factual or intelligent or advisable. It concerns just one, simple, far more basic thing: they feel, however consciously or not, the mortal threat waiting to accost them were they to merely admit: not that certain information is factual, but only that it could be factual. The door to investigating that angle must remain blocked by pretending there’s nothing to investigate. The results of investigating are not the imminent danger. The openness and honesty involved in real investigation are the killers of their blind fidelity to the narrative they’re clinging to for sanity and dear life: the narrative for which, undoubtedly, they have already sacrificed much in order to stay clung.

It’s no wonder that all the most important areas of human life—personal relationships, business, government, and especially those infernal bedfellows religion and the military—revolve around the core of “sacrifice” and are permeated with its theme.

Such people are gruesomely enslaved. We call them “cultists” when they seem wildly strange and different from ourselves, pretending that our own particular enslavement to our own particular survival/salvation narratives is virtuous, while theirs is vile.

There’s a simple, foolproof litmus test for cultism. It tells us where a person’s rationality ends and their cultism begins—including our own:

Mark the point at which a person refuses to look at a possibility for fear that it might turn out to be a fact.

Herbert Spencer’s statement, unwittingly no doubt, captured the hallmark trait of all cultists: zealous disparagement of unwanted information and those who bring it to them for fear of the mere possibility that it might prove to be true.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
I was recently asked, “Given that the authorities keep lying to the people, why do the people keep believing the authorities?”

Well, because when you boil authoritarianism down to its essence and basic structure, it’s incontrovertible: we were all mind-fucked into thinking like cultists.

The foremost aspect of cultism is infantilism. Think about it. To believe authorities requires suspending our own better judgment and knowledge in order to adopt the position of a child before them.

Infantilism guarantees codependence.

Codependence guarantees cultism.

That’s what religious training and “education” are primarily about (and always have been), and that’s why they take so long. University, too. It takes a lotta-lotta work to break down our natural self-confidence and abuse us into relying interminably on others instead of maturing and becoming competent in our own right.

Sure, they taught us stuff, for good or ill—but before they taught us anything worth knowing, and far and away more than they informed us or made us smarter, they conditioned us by both the method of teaching itself (Freire’s “banking model of education” https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banking_model_of_education, by systemic Pavlovian conditioning (seats all in a row that we might as well have been strapped to, bells to signal “passing periods” and mark “tardies”, regimentation throughout, etc.), and above all by authoritarian punishment and reward.

None of that aimed at bettering us in ways that we would agree are better, but rather to better make us venerate and serve our higher-ups.

That was the first 15–20 years of our lives, thanks to virtually every authority in our lives, and it gets reinforced incessantly ever afterwards, known as “socialization”. And anyone who resists the conditioning or rebels against it gets stigmatized as “antisocial”, having a “problem with authority”.

The problem isn’t with people who insist on being independent and free—it’s with everyone else who insists that we must all behave like children and submit/defer to and obey our “leaders”.

For my part: fuck that. They’re not my “leaders”. The only leaders I have are people I choose to follow if and when they demonstrate they’re worth following for a while, until I’ve learned what I needed from them. Anyone who’s worth following will be more than happy when a follower stops following, because they’re competent, so they have no need for followers.

Isn’t that what good parents hope: that their children will leave them, become independent, and eventually surpass them? False leaders (they used to be called “false prophets”) have no intention of being left or surpassed. They require interminable codependence, which means interminable infantilism.

How many authorities have you known who demonstrated their follow-worthy competence before they demanded that you follow them? I’m talking about parents, too. How many so-called “leaders” who presumed authority over us made sure that the choice to follow them was always squarely ours?

We’ve sunk so low that the response I usually get to that is, “But, how could that work? That would end up being a disaster!”

I just shake my head. Among fools, ignorance is taken as the limit of possibility.

Compare how many real leaders you’ve seen to how many would-be authorities demanded obedience from you—not only before demonstrating any competence that would support their demand, but far more often despite grave, repeated, demonstrated incompetence?

Elected leaders, those that they appoint to positions of power, and those that they hire into positions of authority never demonstrate their competence to us. At best, they give us promises, and their success rates in keeping those promises rarely rise above the single-digits.

No wonder, because this is what authority is for in the first place: it enables the incompetent to demand what only the competent should ever dare demand, completely bypassing every question of competence.

But the competent don’t do that, do they? Think of all the seriously competent people you’ve known. How many of them demanded that you obey them, even if just in their areas of competence? How many demanded that you obey them merely because they occupied a position that legitimized their demand wholly apart from any and all question of competence?

Competent people don’t need to demand obedience, because their power lies in being very good at doing things—not this fakery they call “power” which is nothing more than an ability to get others to do for them what they cannot do for themselves.

Authority is what fools and idiots need in order to control the competence of others, because they’ve got no confidence whatsoever in their ability to do it themselves.

Pretty simple, right?

Witness the trillions and probably the quadrillions that have been spent to delude us, "educate"/mind-fuck us, "civilize" us, and impose "law and order" on us by rulers, royals, the so-called "elite", so-called "leaders", and every other type of subhuman/psychopath that have held and still hold themselves above us, as if entitled to control us—all of it extorted from us, calling it "taxes" and "protection" and "security", when if it weren't for them there would be nothing to protect us from or secure us against.

Just witness how difficult and expensive it is to keep their massive webs of lies intact and how easy it is, despite all their efforts, to undermine, subvert, and overthrow them, their so-called "narratives".

That's why it's always been true that if they're pushed too far, defied too badly, exposed too much—or far more often, long before a credible threat materializes, when they get terrified shitless at the mere hint that they might be pushed and defied and exposed—they always resort to the same MO: since they can't touch our souls, they threaten and mutilate and kill our bodies.

So, just like scorpions cannot but do according to their nature, toadies—for fear of harm, pain, injury, and death—all give their souls over to carry scorpions on their backs across the pond, then are astonished by the inevitable deadly sting.

Such have we all been, to one degree or another—most often lock, stock, and barrel.

But the problem isn't our natures. The problem is that we lie about our natures. The only reason we're stuck in an apparently endless, vicious cycle is that we lie about it—which is the single key factor perpetuating the cycle.

Without our lies, we could not pretend that it's necessary and unavoidable to let scorpions climb aboard our backs. What's more, we could swim across the pond and leave them stranded.

It's so easy to see who has sold their souls: everyone who refuses to take the path to freedom under the bullshit excuse that it can't be taken.

Ignorance and incredulity are in no way tantamount to impossibility. Pretending them to be so is just further proof of toadiness.

Toady bullshit is not real and it is not true—the exact same bullshit that every one of us who has started off on that “impossible” path has proven with just our single, first step to be a putrid, malicious lie .

Take taxes. Everyone who pays taxes has funded the genocidal rampage that has been the American Way since the inception of the country—first, on a national stage and, since WW2, on the global stage.

Which indigenous peoples has the US failed to decimate or completely wipe out? Which indigenous culture did it not attack, outlaw, and completely stigmatize or even erase in most cases? Which war and which genocide since 1945 has the US neither instigated nor facilitated nor exacerbated nor waged outright?

All of it funded by American taxpayers who both pretend to be sinless and to have no other choice.

Liars.

comment.body:
Codependence is no mystery; nor is it vague or difficult to identify.

Codependence is our still-active infantilism demanding that others change their behavior so that we won’t feel badly—getting upset and punishing them if they refuse.

Codependence isn’t difficult to spot: it’s glaring to everyone except the infantile.

What glitch of logic or failure of reason gives the codependent the idea that others are responsible for their (the codependent’s) feelings?

None.

To glitch or fail, logic and reason would have had to be in the picture in the first place.

That’s precisely what infantilism is: good sense overruled or abolished by instinct, psychopathology, and habit.

Oodles of people have sworn to me up and down that this overruling and abolishing of good sense is inevitable and unavoidable.

Those people are fools. 

And given how easy it is to see that belief for what it is—bullshit (if we even want to see)—they’re liars, too.
